source_text: Οὐκ ἰδοὺ Ἄχαρ ὁ τοῦ Ζαρᾶ πλημμελείᾳ ἐπλημμέλησεν ἀπὸ τοῦ ἀναθέματος, καὶ ἐπὶ πᾶσαν συναγωγὴν Ἰσραήλ ἐγενήθη ἡ ὀργή; καὶ εἷς μόνος οὗτος ἥμαρτε, μὴ μόνος ἀπέθανεν ἐν τῇ ἁμαρτίᾳ αὐτοῦ; Ἡμῖν δὲ πᾶν τὸ μὴ ἡμέτερον, ἀλλὰ ἀλλότριον τῷ καιρῷ τούτῳ κέρδος, ἀνάθεμα νενομίσθαι προσήκει. Κἀκεῖνος μὲν γὰρ ὁ Ἄχαρ, ἐκ τῆς προνομῆς ἔλαβε· καὶ αὐτοὶ νῦν ἐκ προνομῆς. Κἀκεῖνος μὲν τὰ τῶν πολεμίων· οἱ δὲ νῦν τὰ τῶν ἀδελφῶν, κερδάναντες ὀλέθριον κέρδος.
thought_title: Warning against profiteering from the suffering of fellow believers
orientation: Gregory warns that greed at this moment is anathema, drawing on the example of Achan whose single sin brought wrath on all Israel, and contrasts Achan's plunder of enemies with the current plundering of brothers.
pass_a_gloss: Behold, did not Achan son of Zerah sin with respect to the devoted thing, and did wrath come upon all the assembly of Israel? And this one alone sinned; did not he alone die in his sin? But for us, every gain that is not ours but foreign at this time ought to be considered anathema. For that Achan took from the spoil; and these now from spoil. That one took the things of enemies; but these now the things of brothers, gaining destructive gain.

choices.why: Cognate accusative construction emphasizing the offense; matches LXX Joshua 7:1 language about Achan's transgression of the ban.
Technical term for property placed under divine ban (herem); Achan took from the spoil of Jericho which was devoted to destruction.

choices.english: gain that is not ours but foreign at this time
choices.why: Contrasts legitimate vs illegitimate profit; 'foreign' captures ἀλλότριος as belonging to another, not merely 'strange'.
προσήκει expresses moral necessity; νενομίσθαι passive 'be deemed/reckoned'; the gain itself is to be treated as devoted to destruction.
Sharp contrast with τὰ τῶν πολεμίων; the profiteers are plundering fellow Christians, not enemies.
ὀλέθριος implies ruinous character; the profit destroys the soul of the gainer.

bible_refs.note: Achan son of Zerah took from the devoted things and wrath fell on all Israel
Achan alone sinned but he alone died in his sin (though household also perished)
The spoil of Jericho was devoted to the Lord; taking from it brought the ban

pass_b_english: Consider Achan son of Zerah: he sinned by sinning against the devoted thing, and wrath came upon the whole assembly of Israel. He alone sinned, yet he did not die alone in his sin. For us, any gain that is not ours but belongs to another at this time ought to be considered a devoted thing. That Achan took from the spoil of the enemies; these people now take from the spoil of brothers, gaining destructive profit.
